analysis.subject: earth-science
analysis.pageCoverage: The source presents a table of physical properties, orbital characteristics, temperature, pressure, moons, rings and magnetic field for worlds orbiting the Sun.

overview.headline: Comparing physical and orbital properties of solar system worlds

keyPoints.point: Students learn that orbital period grows longer for worlds farther from the Sun.
Students learn that mean temperature generally decreases for outer worlds.
Students learn that surface pressure varies widely across different worlds.
keyPoints.quote: | Surface Pressure (bars) | 0 | 92 | 1 | 0 | 0.01 | Unknown* | Unknown* | Unknown* | Unknown* | 0.00001 |

keyPoints.point: Students learn that a global magnetic field is present for some worlds and absent for others.
keyPoints.quote: | Global Magnetic Field? | Yes | No | Yes | No | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Unknown |

keyTerms.gloss: Time needed for a world to complete one orbital journey around the Sun
Average temperature value that characterises a world surface or atmosphere
Pressure exerted by the atmosphere at the world surface
keyTerms.quote: | Surface Pressure (bars) | 0 | 92 | 1 | 0 | 0.01 | Unknown* | Unknown* | Unknown* | Unknown* | 0.00001 |

keyTerms.gloss: Collection of particles forming a ring structure around a world
keyTerms.quote: | Ring System? | No | No | No | No | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |

keyTerms.gloss: Large scale magnetic region generated by a world interior
keyTerms.quote: | Global Magnetic Field? | Yes | No | Yes | No | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Unknown |

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Helps students compare quantitative properties across worlds in one organized view.
